canonical_sequence: Rowan Pike prepared a polarized insert from a catalog image before the gala.
Rowan entered Gallery 3 alone under the authorized catalog work order.
While the case was in calibration mode, Rowan taped over the rear contact sensor and opened the service panel.
Rowan removed Aurora Circuit at 2026-08-30T04:42:18Z and placed the polarized insert in the display guide.
Rowan moved the 1.84-kilogram sculpture into his hard equipment case and checked that case into the media locker.
The scheduled blackout later exposed the empty display and misdirected attention toward the lighting system.

claim_rules.description: The artwork was removed before the planned blackout.
The rear service-panel contact was deliberately bypassed.
A polarized image concealed the empty display from the gala viewing line.
Rowan was the only suspect with access at the actual removal time.
Rowan's statement about remaining three meters away conflicts with his camera record.
Rowan's hard case gained the artwork's exact mass before locker intake.
The blackout executed automatically rather than through a manual console command.
Independent recordings place Mara, Theo, and Nia away from Gallery 3 at the removal time.

exoneration_rules.summary: The real removal occurred while Mara was continuously visible in the greenroom.
Theo was in the lighting booth at the removal time, and the later blackout was automatic.
Nia's body camera places her at the loading bay when the plinth lost its load.

hints: Treat the blackout as the discovery time, not necessarily the theft time.
Compare the plinth's weight change with the Gallery 3 access window.
Compare Aurora Circuit's mass with the photographer's equipment-case records.
